observations.seen: The white and teal bike and astronaut read almost uniformly bright in every frame, with no clear key-light side or form shading. The large pale moon/sun sits on the horizon but casts no visible warm directional light across the track or rocks. The scene is a purple nebula night, not the golden-hour low-sun look the recipe expects.
No cast shadows are visible from the bike, poles, rocks or track supports. Frame 1 shows only a faint purple smudge under the bike, so the vehicle looks pasted onto the terracotta surface.
Frame 1 has a soft, low-detail moon reflection on the left of the track surface. The bike body looks matte and shows no environment reflections or specular highlights from the nebula sky.

The world has a consistent theme: a nebula skybox, a ribbon track with white marker lights, a harp-like arch and floating low-poly rocks. It is sparse, though. Orange poles repeat with little variation, and the maroon mountains are a flat silhouette band without depth layering.

Distant mountains and the far track stay as crisp and saturated as the near geometry, so there is no visible 30–180 m distance fog or haze. The only atmosphere comes from the painted nebula sky and scattered star particles.

The track has a mottled terracotta texture that looks smeared and low-resolution up close (frames 1 and 2). Rocks are flat-shaded and untextured. The bike's white panels are blown out, so the material shows no detail.
The sidecar bike and astronaut have reasonable mid-poly shapes with wheels and a visible suit. The rocks are basic faceted polyhedra and the poles are plain tapered cylinders.

Frame 1 balances the moon on the left against the bike on the right. Frame 3 centers the bike in empty starfield with rocks scattered at random. In frame 4 the countdown '3' overlaps the moon, the one focal element.

The chase framing in frame 2 puts the subject at about 15–20% of the frame, which matches the recipe. In frame 3 the camera has drifted off the track into open space with no track reference, which weakens the sense of speed and direction.

Frame 1 shows a vignette and soft overall blur, and frame 4 adds letterbox bars. The bright bike looks clipped rather than tone-mapped, there is no film grain or warm cinematic grade, and no motion blur at 137–199 km/h.

The HUD panels share one clean dark style and stay readable: position, lap, race time, leaderboard and speedometer. The centered instruction text floats over the scene with no backing, and in frame 4 the top panels sit on top of the letterbox bars.

nextChange.change: raise shadow strength toward the look target and pull the key light to an angle that throws visible contact shadows
